title: DSA - Why Quicksort? + Time Complexity
description:
## Why Quicksort?
You've now built bubble sort, insertion sort, merge sort, and quicksort. Here's how they compare:

| Algorithm | Best | Average | Worst | Space | In-place? |
|-----------|------|---------|-------|-------|-----------|
| Bubble Sort | O(n) | O(n²) | O(n²) | O(1) | Yes |
| Insertion Sort | O(n) | O(n²) | O(n²) | O(1) | Yes |
| Merge Sort | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n) | No |
| Quicksort | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n²) | O(1) | Yes |

Quicksort wins in practice because:
- **In-place** - no extra arrays like merge sort
- **Cache friendly** - works on contiguous memory
- **O(n log n) average** - worst case is rare with random pivot
- **Low overhead** - less bookkeeping than merge sort

That's why `std::sort` in C++ uses a hybrid of quicksort, insertion sort, and heapsort (called Introsort).

---
## Question:
Quicksort and merge sort both average O(n log n). Why is quicksort faster in practice?
b2t: In-place sorting and better cache performance
